cards.text: Moses just met God at a burning bush, and his orders are clear: Egypt (Exodus 3:2-10). So first he goes back to his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian (Exodus 3:1). He asks him, “Please let me return to my brothers in Egypt to see if they are still alive.”

cards.question: Jethro tells Moses to stay in Midian a little while longer.

cards.text: Now here's a detail. Back in Midian, the LORD had already told Moses it was safe to go back, and friend, Moses did NOT leave Egypt on good terms (Exodus 2:15).

cards.question: Why does the LORD say it's safe for Moses to go back to Egypt?

answers.text: The men who wanted to kill him are dead
Pharaoh has forgiven what he did years ago
The Israelites have promised to hide him

cards.text: So Moses puts his wife and sons on a donkey and heads for Egypt. A whole family on ONE donkey? Friend, I lived in a junk drawer for YEARS, and even I'm looking at that saying, “That's tight.”

cards.question: Moses heads for Egypt with the ___ of God in his hand.

cards.text: Then the LORD instructs Moses for when he gets back to Egypt. In front of Pharaoh, Moses is to perform ALL the wonders the LORD has put in his power.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses that once Pharaoh sees the wonders, he'll let the people go right away.

cards.text: The LORD says it plainly: He will harden Pharaoh's heart so that he will not let the people go. Then He gives Moses a message for Pharaoh, and it's all about Israel.

cards.question: In His message for Pharaoh, what does the LORD call Israel?

cards.text: The message goes on: God told Pharaoh to let His son go so he can worship Him, and Pharaoh has refused. Moses has to say this to PHARAOH, friend, and I couldn't even work up the nerve to ask the shiny new stamper to scoot over!

cards.question: Since Pharaoh refuses to let God's son go, what does the LORD say He'll do?

cards.text: Then, at a lodging place along the way, something shocking happens. The LORD meets Moses and is about to kill him.

cards.question: Moses' life is on the line at that lodging place. Who steps in?

cards.text: Zipporah grabs a flint knife, circumcises her son and touches the foreskin to Moses' feet. She says, “Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me,” and that line is about the circumcision.

cards.question: After Zipporah acts, the LORD lets Moses alone.

cards.text: Meanwhile, the LORD tells Aaron, Moses' brother, “Go and meet Moses in the wilderness.” That's the WHOLE address. No pin, no landmark, no “turn left at the big rock,” and Aaron just GOES.

cards.question: Where do Aaron and Moses finally meet up?

answers.text: On the banks of the Nile

cards.text: Aaron sees his brother and kisses him. The last time I saw my family, a drawer closed between us, so friend, this one gets me right in the dough.

cards.question: Moses keeps the signs to himself and lets Aaron find out at the big meeting.

cards.text: Then Moses and Aaron gather all the elders of the Israelites. I bet Moses has been sweating this moment since the burning bush, like walking into a meeting and finding out YOU are the whole agenda.

cards.question: With the elders gathered, who relays everything the LORD said to Moses?
While Aaron does the talking, Moses performs the ___ before the people.
After hearing the LORD's words and seeing the signs, how do the people respond?
When the people hear that the LORD has seen their affliction, they ___ down and ___.

cards.text: Hold that thought, friend, and keep the oven warm, because this story is FAR from finished.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 10 cites "", which is not a BSB reference.

rule.text: verses: what the card cites. On a choice card, it is only the verses of the right answer.

findings.problem: "A whole family on ONE donkey?" puts Moses on the donkey too. Exodus 4:20 says only that Moses put his wife and sons on a donkey. The joke is built on a detail the text doesn't give, so it reads as a stretched fact rather than an exaggeration inside his own joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "I couldn't even work up the nerve to ask the shiny new stamper to scoot over!" invents a new moment in the Millers' kitchen. In the backstory he never deals with the new stamper. He is simply moved to the drawer. The line also depends on the baker knowing about the replacement stamper, which no earlier card sets up.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Aaron is introduced as "Moses' brother." That fact comes from outside the passage (Exodus 4:14) but has no reference. Stop 1 card 1 gives references for its outside facts, and this card should too.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The comparison is "walking into a meeting and finding out YOU are the whole agenda." That is about being surprised. Moses isn't surprised: he and Aaron called the meeting themselves (Exodus 4:29), and Aaron does the talking (4:30). The everyday image doesn't match the core action, which is facing a gathering he planned.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "sleep" gives silly combinations like "bow down and sleep" or "sit down and sleep" in response to the LORD seeing their affliction. It doesn't match the tone of the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "___ down and ___" asks the baker to fill in the wording of a set phrase. "Bow down" versus "sit down" is a wording guess, not a question of meaning. A question about how the people respond to the news would test meaning instead.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The closing story card is only the "story isn't over" line, which the docs allow. Its "verses" field is an empty string.
findings.question: When a closing story card tells no verses, should its "verses" field be empty, repeat the last verse of the stop, or be left out?
